sentences.text: Machimosaurus teeth are characterized by a rounded, blunt apex and stout morphology, making them easily distinguishable from other teleosaurid teeth. Morphological comparisons of its teeth confirm Machimosaurus was adapted to capture and crush hard prey.

Vertebrae articulations indicate Machimosaurus lived in open seas, swimming via lateral tail undulations while using limbs for steering and balance. Based on vertebrae zygapophysis joints, Machimosaurus likely lived in open seas, swimming with lateral tail undulations while its legs steered and balanced the body.

Machimosaurus is the largest known crocodyliform from the Jurassic period. Machimosaurus rex, described in 2016 from Tunisia, is the largest known teleosaurid, estimated at 9.6 meters long and weighing nearly three tons.

Bite marks on a sauropod femur from Switzerland match teeth of Machimosaurus hugii, suggesting it fed on sauropods. Bite marks on a Cetiosauriscus femur from the early Kimmeridgian of Switzerland match the known teeth of Machimosaurus hugii. Fossil turtles from the Kimmeridgian Solothurn Limestone in northern Switzerland show bite marks and contain chipped Machimosaurus teeth embedded in their shells.
Machimosaurus went extinct during the Hauterivian, making it the last of the teleosaurids. Machimosaurus rex represents the most recent record of a teleosaurid, originating from the Early Cretaceous.

The genus Machimosaurus was named by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1837. Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer originally named isolated conical, blunt teeth from Switzerland as Madrimosaurus hugii in 1837. In 1838, von Meyer corrected the misspelling to Machimosaurus, derived from Greek words meaning "pugnacious lizard".

Fossils of Machimosaurus have been found in the semi-aquatic deposits of Oker, Lower Saxony, Germany, dating to the Kimmeridgian age. Machimosaurus is also found alongside Steneosaurus in Titonian age deposits in western France.
Morphofunctional analysis of the skull suggests Machimosaurus specialized in eating turtles. Morphofunctional analysis of the skull suggests Machimosaurus regularly ate turtles.

The genus includes species such as M. hugii, M. mosae, M. nowackianus, M. buffetauti, and M. rex. Machimosaurus belongs to the family Teleosauridae and the subfamily Machimosaurini. It is classified within the suborder Thalattosuchia. Some sources also classify it within the family Machimosauridae.

Machimosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian and Tithonian) and Early Cretaceous periods. Machimosaurus lived between the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian and Tithonian) and Early Cretaceous (Berriasian and Hauterivian) periods. Machimosaurus lived between 165.3 and 113.2 million years ago during the Callovian to Aptian periods. Fossils of Machimosaurus have been found in Switzerland, England, France, Germany, Portugal, and Tunisia.
It is uncertain whether ichnofossils of a gigantic crocodylomorph from Spain belong to Machimosaurus.
